statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 6% (low), Stress 63% (elevated), Confidence 76% (high).
recommendation: Tail sits near its floor because CME equity-index futures are halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to trend. Stress remains elevated on the unresolved US-Iran tanker exchange and crude at six-week highs. The single flagged window is the 22:00Z Globex restart, where Tail is mapped to WATCH for one hour.
headline: Futures halted for Labor Day; risk concentrated at the 22:00Z Globex restart
body: CME equity-index futures halted at 17:00Z (12:00 CT) and resume at 22:00Z, while NYSE and Nasdaq stayed shut all day for Labor Day. The last NQ print was 29,565.25, up 40.50 points (+0.14%), inside a narrow 29,530.50-29,682.50 holiday range having faded from the session high, so the pre-halt tape showed working retracements and no one-way structure. There is now no live order book at all, which removes price-path risk for the next five hours but also removes the evidence on which a forward path read would normally rest. The live risk is energy and geopolitical: Brent is near $97.28, up about 1.0% and at six-week highs, with WTI around $93, after US Central Command destroyed or disabled three Iranian tankers and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed retaliatory attacks on three tankers and three US-linked vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler-tracked transits are reported at roughly 13 vessels a day against about 20 million barrels flowing before the conflict, and Iranian officials signalled on Sunday that proportionate responses are over. VIX last printed 15.30 at Friday's close and Treasury yields last printed 4.34% at two years and 4.77% at ten years in the 3 September H.15 data; neither updates on the holiday. That combination - a benign equity backdrop against a genuine energy and shipping shock - is cross-asset conflict, which widens uncertainty without producing the persistent no-retracement path that defines Tail. The identified structural risk is mechanical rather than directional: five hours of unpriced escalation headlines clearing into a thin restart at 22:00Z, which is why the danger window is one hour rather than session-wide. A secondary checkpoint is the 13:30Z Tuesday cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend. The week's principal macro risk sits Thursday with PPI and jobless claims and Friday with August CPI. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was available but timestamped 13:03Z, beyond the freshness limit, so it was not used as supporting evidence for this assessment.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available; the 2026-09-06T21:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The window was uniformly green with EA_ON throughout and Tail between 5% and 10%. Stress rose from a 54-58% band overnight to 61-64% during the US afternoon as crude extended and holiday liquidity thinned. Confidence eased from 86% to 79% over the same stretch. Dominant mode was normal except the 14:00Z and 16:00Z slots, which were mixed as the energy-versus-equity divergence widened into the halt.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are shaped by market structure rather than macro. Futures are halted until 22:00Z, so the first five forecast hours carry no tradable price path and Tail sits at its floor. The single elevated slot is the 22:00Z restart, where five hours of unpriced US-Iran escalation would meet the thinnest liquidity of the window; Tail is mapped to WATCH there for one hour only. Path risk then decays through the Asian and European sessions as depth rebuilds, with a secondary rise into the 13:30Z US cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend. All post-halt structure is framed conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff; only the pre-halt range and fade are stated as fact. NFIB at 10:00Z is the sole scheduled US release inside the window, and the week's principal checkpoints - PPI and jobless claims Thursday, August CPI Friday - fall outside it.
